hooks.text: Billions of starless rogue planets drift through total darkness.
What happens when a planet is violently flung into deep space?
Seventy rogue planets were discovered in a single star-forming region.

title: Billions of Starless Rogue Planets Drift in Darkness
description: Discover how billions of starless rogue planets wander through the Milky Way without a sun.

beats.text: Billions of starless rogue planets drift through total darkness.

beats.text: These strange worlds roam across the vast expanse of the Milky Way galaxy entirely alone.
beats.visual: milky way galaxy artist concept showing stellar expanse, 2019

beats.text: Free-floating planetary masses are not bound to any star or brown dwarf.
beats.visual: Orion Nebula infrared view showing star-forming region, 2006

beats.text: Some form on their own within stellar nurseries, while others are violently ejected from natal systems.
beats.visual: planet-planet scattering illustration showing exoplanet ejection, 2018

beats.text: In December twenty twenty-one, astronomers found a group of up to one hundred seventy rogue planets.
beats.visual: Very Large Telescope Paranal view during laser guide star operation, 2015

beats.text: In September twenty twenty, astronomers reported the detection of an Earth-mass rogue planet named OGLE-2016-BLG-1928.
beats.visual: gravitational microlensing diagram explaining exoplanet detection, 2019

beats.text: NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope will use microlensing to reveal hundreds more.
